messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike in 5xx and gateway timeouts for region eu-west1 (gateway-frontend). 1m error rate > 12% across customer-facing routes for redwood-13b. Paging oncall.
maya: oncall here, looking. seeing 524s + 502s. dashboard: https://console.redwood/internal/alerts/1839123456
ben: I’m pulled in. any recent deploys to eu-west1? infra-bot, did we get a new rollout? :eyes:
infra-bot: Deploy: service/gateway-frontend v2.14.7 rolled to eu-west1 at 2026-03-14T03:08:12Z (triggered by canary automation). No autoscaler changes.
maya: logs show persistent upstream timeouts to inference pool: "upstream request timeout after 60s" from gateway -> inference-proxy-eu-west1
maya: quick dump:
```
[2026-03-14T03:12:41Z] gateway-frontend eu-west1 - route=/v1/generate - status=524 - downstream_latency_ms=60014 - upstream=kvcache-proxy-3 - up_error=timeout
[2026-03-14T03:12:42Z] gateway-frontend eu-west1 - status=502 - upstream=dedicated-pool-1 - err=connection_reset
```
priya: I’m on network infra. checking inter-region links and LB health.
leo: Can we fail traffic to eu-central? Routing policy supports region failover. We should prefer eu-central until we have stable upstream.
maya: agree. mitigation plan:
  1) flip routing policy for customer-tier=prod to prefer eu-central for redwood-13b (failover window 10m)
  2) increase dedicated-pool-1 replica count in eu-central by +2
  3) temporarily lower rate limit for best-effort customers to reduce load
  4) monitor errors and latency. rollback if errors increase
ben: I can run the routing change. executing now:
```
#cli
redwood route update --model redwood-13b --region-preference eu-central,eu-west1 --failover-window 600
```
ben: done. traffic shift started at 03:16:05Z. currently 18% of prod traffic still hitting eu-west (draining).
priya: network checks: detected intermittent packet loss on eu-west1 egress to storage cluster (multihop) starting 03:10Z. a subset of inference nodes lost connectivity to remote KV cache. working with cloud provider.
maya: that explains upstream timeouts to kvcache-proxy. switching to local cache variant might reduce remote calls. Leo, can we enable cache-localized config for gateway in eu-central/backup?
leo: yes, pushing config change to prefer local-kv when remote latency > 50ms. pushing now.
```
#config
gateway.frontend.kv_strategy=prefer_local_on_latency
```
leo: config rollout initiated.
sally-cs: FYI a few paying customers reported request failures via support. I informed them we’re mitigating and will update in 15m.
maya: scaling eu-central pool now (ben can confirm replicas):
ben: scaling command:
```
kubectl scale deployment ded-pool-1 -n eu-central --replicas=8
```
ben: replicas increased from 6 -> 8 at 03:18:40Z. warmup in progress.
maya: telemetry after routing change (03:20Z):
  - overall 5xx rate dropped to 6%
  - eu-west1 5xx still 20% (draining)
  - eu-central 5xx 1.2%
maya: good. customer-visible errors decreasing. keep the failover for 30m and track provider updates.
priya: provider sent maintenance note: "intermittent egress degradation affecting select subnets". ETA unknown. they opened support ticket 987654.
leo: setting automatic fallback policy to route to eu-central when gateway 5xx > 8% for 5m. that will automate future flips.
```
#policy
redwood.routing.fallback.threshold=8
redwood.routing.fallback.duration=300
```
maya: can someone run a canary synthetic against eu-west1 to see if any healthy backend nodes remain?
ben: running canary now -> results: 3/10 succeed with high latency. not reliable.
maya: ok, keep routing pref eu-central. start throttling free-tier: reduce qps by 40% for non-paid keys to buy headroom.
ben: applied quota patch at 03:26:10Z.
```
#quota
policy.free-tier.max_qps *= 0.6
```
sally-cs: updated customers with note: "We routed traffic to alternate region to mitigate timeouts. Some requests served from eu-central; latency may be slightly higher for affected users." :thumbsup:
priya: provider now indicates partial restoration on some subnets at 03:30Z. they’re probing.
maya: metrics at 03:34Z: global 5xx 3.7% ; eu-west1 9.8% ; user-impacted requests trending down. re-evaluate in 20m.
leo: starting handoff checklist for night oncall if this persists: assign priyasingh for followups, set postmortem owner, capture timeline.
maya: assigning postmortem to priya
priya: ack. I’ll own the postmortem and coordinate with provider.
ben: should we advertise a maintenance note on status.redwood.com? sally can push a short blurb.
sally-cs: posting maintenance update: "Partial degradation in eu-west1 causing intermittent request failures. We’ve routed traffic to eu-central; most customers are restored. Full update in 1h." Posted 03:38Z.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03-14-4123, severity=high, link: https://incidents.redwood/internal/INC-4123
maya: summary for now: cause = provider egress/subnet packet loss impacting KV cache access in eu-west1 -> gateway upstream timeouts -> elevated 5xx. mitigation = routing failover to eu-central, local-kv config fallback, scale eu-central pool, throttle free tier. customer impact: ~12% of prod requests failed at peak; now <4% global. next steps: provider followup, postmortem, make fallback policy permanent? discuss in postmortem.
priya: provider assigned engineer, they’ll follow up with root-cause. I’ll include trace logs in incident ticket.
leo: leaving note for oncall handoff at 03:44Z: if eu-west1 5xx > 7% for 10m re-run failover and escalate to infra lead.
maya: handing off to night oncall (priya). I’ll remain reachable for questions. paging out.
priya: taking over. last checks: monitoring alerts set, runbook link added: https://runbooks.redwood/kv-egress-deg
maya: thanks team. logging the timeline and closing paging. we’ll cut postmortem draft tomorrow.
incident-bot: RESOLVE: alert condition cleared at 03:48:42Z (global 5xx < 2% for 10m). Incident INC-2026-03-14-4123 remains open for postmortem and provider RCA.
maya: resolved for paging, leaving incident open for postmortem.
